intro: Glitches and odd mechanics found while studying the games behind the brawler: what the player does, what happens, and why in the game's own code. Measured in emulators from each game's program. Some of these made the games what they are.

quirks.title: The air fury
quirks.do: In the air with full POWER, Ryo enters his fury motion (Kim: his fury with B+D).
quirks.happens: The fury comes out in mid-air (Ryo's Haoh Shoukou Ken, Kim's Houou Kyaku).
quirks.why: Each frame three routines run in order: the picker ($76E6) starts the highest ready move; the recogniser ($B2C0) marks every command the input completes and checks each one's condition; the MAX timer counts down ($952C). Ryo's C completes both his air fireball 236P (slot 6) and his fury 2363214C (slot 7) on the same frame. The air fireball's condition ($B53A) raises an 'allowed in the air' flag (+$E5 bit 6) that is one flag for the whole fighter, not tied to its slot. The fury's condition ($B592: power 127 or life <= 64) never checks the air, and the picker takes the highest slot: the fury. Kim: B+D completes his fury and also counts as K for his air 236K.
quirks.brawler: A deliberate version needs a per-move 'allowed in the air' flag checked on the move that actually starts.

shots.caption: Ryo's fury in the air (every 2 frames)

quirks.title: The glitch inside the glitch: a ground special in the air
quirks.do: The same air fury input, on the exact frame the MAXIMUM bar runs out.
quirks.happens: Ryo performs Hien Shippu Kyaku in mid-air; Kim performs Hangetsuzan in mid-air.
quirks.why: The fury starts, but its handler re-checks the power on entry (jsr $4918). The MAX timer hit 0 on that very frame (power 127 -> 125), so the check fails and the handler jumps hard-wired to a regular special (Ryo $2C3FA -> $2BC3C, Kim $23E8C -> $23906) — which never checks the air either. One-frame window: one frame earlier gives the normal air fireball, one frame later the fury. Life must be above 64.
quirks.brawler: Power should be taken once when a move commits, and fallbacks declared explicitly.

shots.caption: Left: the fury in the air at MAXIMUM. Right: the MAX timer ran out on the input frame — a ground special in the air

quirks.title: The air fury for Robert, Mai and Kensou (the jump-normal method)
quirks.do: Robert: jump, kick with D, and while the kick is out do the Haoh Shoukou Ken motion with C, then tap D. Mai: jump with a D kick, her fury motion with B+C, then tap A. Kensou: jump with an A punch, then 4-2-1-3-6-4-6 with D, then C.
quirks.happens: The fury comes out in mid-air. Let MAXIMUM run out between the presses and the fallback comes out in the air instead (Robert Hien Shippu Kyaku, Mai Hissatsu Shinobibachi, Kensou his 41236P) — a ~5-frame window, easier than Ryo's 1-frame one.
quirks.why: A jump normal holds a 'special move allowed' window open (+$7C bit 5) and blocks new jump normals. The fury button goes in first: the fury is queued but can't start (no air flag). The air move's button arrives 4 frames later (input buffer) and completes the air special, raising the fighter-wide 'allowed in the air' flag; the next picker run takes the highest queued move — the fury. A queued command lives 3 frames per command completed that frame, so the fury press must complete two commands at once to outlast the 4-frame delay (Robert's C also completes 236P; Kensou's reordered motion makes D finish 421K too). Found by Bruno as a player; confirmed in captures.

shots.caption: KOF95: all five characters with the air fury (Ryo, Kim, Robert, Mai, Kensou)

quirks.title: The glitch inside the glitch works on the ground too — and Yuri's mystery move
quirks.do: Enter a fury on the exact frame the MAXIMUM bar runs out, standing on the ground.
quirks.happens: Each character performs a fixed regular special instead (Ryo: Hien Shippu Kyaku without its charge). Yuri does a short hop kick that is not one of her command moves.
quirks.why: Every fury handler re-checks the power on entry ($4918) and, on failure, jumps to a hard-wired fallback: Heidern [2]8K, Ralf / Chang / Choi [4]6P, Athena 214P, Kensou 41236P, Kyo / Benimaru / Chin 623P, Iori / Eiji / King 63214K, Kim 214K, Terry [2]8P, Andy 16K, Joe 2369K, Ryo / Robert / Takuma Hien Shippu Kyaku, Mai 41236K, Saisyu 236P, Omega Rugal 63214P, Billy his PPPP mash. Yuri's points at $2F536 (KOF94 $29D70): states 112-114, a hop that no input reaches otherwise. On the ground it looks like an ordinary move, so nobody noticed. The air version only exists for Ryo and Kim: no other character's fury input also completes an air move on one press (the second button arrives 4 frames late, after a jump normal has started), and Athena's / Choi's fury refuses the air outright.

shots.caption: Yuri: fury input on the MAX-expiry frame on the ground → the hidden hop move ($2F536)

quirks.title: The air fury, KOF94 version
quirks.do: Ryo: 2 3 6 2 4 then C on a neutral stick, in the air at full power. Kim: his fury only at the very top of his jump.
quirks.happens: The same air fury and the same one-frame ground-special fallback, with differences.
quirks.why: Same design (recogniser $AF78, picker $7796, power re-check $4C0E, timer $9340). Ryo's air 236P must end on a remembered forward, hence the odd input. Kim's air move is 2K, only allowed near the jump's apex (vertical speed within +-2), so his air fury works only there; his fallback Hangetsuzan floats at one height, then snaps to the ground. Robert's KOF94 fury checks that it is airborne and plays his air 21K instead — KOF95 dropped that guard. Fury life threshold 63 instead of 64.

shots.caption: KOF94: Ryo and Kim, air fury and the power-out fallback

quirks.title: The thrown body refills your chain
quirks.do: With Haggar: jab, jab, back + punch (backdrop) — then on another enemy just one jab and back + punch throws again.
quirks.happens: The second throw comes after a single jab instead of two.
quirks.why: The throw resets the chain, but when the thrown body lands on another enemy or object the game credits that hit to the thrower: his 45-frame chain credit refills, so the next jab already counts as link 2 and the following press is the final link (the throw). Never on the same enemy (the downed one is untouchable ~150 frames). Haggar's backdrop drops the body ~70 px behind him, often onto someone; Guy and Cody throw ~186 px, so it happens less.
quirks.brawler: Proposed to keep on purpose: a hit by your thrown body counts as your hit.

shots.caption: Haggar's backdrop from the chain (every 2 frames)

quirks.title: The 'half second' before an enemy hits
quirks.do: Stand near an enemy and watch it.
quirks.happens: It seems to start attacking but the hit takes a long time to come.
quirks.why: Before most attacks the enemy holds its ordinary stance for a random wait taken from a table (1 to 60 frames, about half a second on average), then swings with a short wind-up (3-6 frames for punches, 12-15 for knives and charges, 20-50 for special moves). The warning you can read is only on the big hits.
quirks.brawler: Proposed: keep the random wait but show a distinct ready pose during it.

shots.caption: Bred: hold, wind-up, active
Andore: 49-frame clinch before the throw

quirks.title: A hidden difficulty rank
quirks.do: Nothing visible.
quirks.happens: Enemy count, health and damage change during play.
quirks.why: A RAM byte ($FF80A8) is a hidden rank that sets how many enemies spawn and their health and damage; each enemy also reads its damage table from a later start point as the game goes on (Bred's punch 4, 5, 6, 7, 8...).

quirks.title: Fast or slow finisher, decided by timing
quirks.do: Press the 4th attack of the combo right as the 3rd hit recovers, or a little later.
quirks.happens: Pressed within 2 frames: a 2-hit finisher; later: a single-hit finisher.
quirks.why: The combo code checks how soon the 4th press comes after recovery; all four fighters have both versions (Axel 10 + 14 vs 10).
quirks.brawler: Proposed as a rhythm reward: one extra route for a sharp press.

shots.caption: Axel's combo

quirks.title: Max and Axel share the same jump, bit for bit
quirks.do: Jump forward with Axel and with Max.
quirks.happens: Axel seems to move forward a frame or two sooner.
quirks.why: Their arcs and air acceleration are identical to the sub-pixel; the only difference is the sub-pixel fraction each starts from (Axel walks 1.25 px per frame, so he can carry 0.75 px into the jump; Max walks 1.0 and stays on whole pixels). Both cover 69 px.

quirks.title: Dutch's buffer is a trap
quirks.do: With Dutch, press the next attack during the hit freeze.
quirks.happens: The next hit comes out later than if you had pressed just after the freeze.
quirks.why: Dutch is the only character whose presses during hit-stop are kept — but they fire at the end of the animation, not at the first frame you could act.
quirks.brawler: Proposed: a buffer for everyone, firing at the first possible frame.

shots.caption: Dutch's combo

quirks.title: Juggles with a brake
quirks.do: Launch an alien and keep hitting it in the air.
quirks.happens: After 3 air hits it can't be touched; the more juggle hits it took, the faster it gets up.
quirks.why: A stun meter per enemy fills with hits and the finisher always launches; each air hit pops the alien a little and adds 1 to a juggle counter capped at 3; lying time shrinks with the counter.
quirks.brawler: Proposed: the same launch model, a built-in brake against endless juggles.

shots.caption: Linn: chain, launch, 3 juggle hits to the cap

quirks.title: Mash to extend Yashiro's fury
quirks.do: During Yashiro's punch-rush super, keep pressing A or C.
quirks.happens: More hits: 5 unmashed, 13 mashed (MAX: 7 vs 23).
quirks.why: Every frame of the flurry the code reads a new A / C press and sets a latch; when the flurry ends, a set latch replays it, at most 4 times (MAX 8). Ralf's Vulcan Punch, Billy's CCCC spins and Mr. Big's punches (KOF96) work the same way.
quirks.brawler: Yashiro plays the maxed-out rush as standard since 0.4.0 (Bruno's call); the others are left as they are.

shots.caption: Yashiro's fury, mashed: 13 hits

quirks.title: Steer a throw after starting it
quirks.do: Grab, press forward+B, then hold UP (or the other direction) while the throw animates: the enemy is thrown BEHIND you instead of in front (lands 160 px behind instead of 218 px ahead).
quirks.why: The throw reads the stick at its release frame, not at the press: holding UP flips the facing, LEFT/RIGHT set it ($1a88c).

shots.caption: Steer a throw after starting it

quirks.title: Landing lag disappears if you hold a direction
quirks.do: A neutral jump lands with 7 frames of recovery; holding any direction as you land skips them and you walk at once.
quirks.why: The landing state hands over to the walk code whenever the stick is not neutral.

shots.caption: Landing lag disappears if you hold a direction

quirks.title: Enemies take less damage as they get weaker
quirks.do: The same jab does 10 to a full-life soldier, 9 at 40 life, 7 at 20, 4 at 7: the last hits on any enemy do less.
quirks.why: Below 64 life the victim gets a damage reduction from a small table (20/32 at life < 8), applied as if it were extra defense ($1be0).

shots.caption: Enemies take less damage as they get weaker

quirks.title: Desperation damage for everyone
quirks.do: At 16 life or less, attacks gain random bonus damage (jab 10 -> 10 or 11, bigger moves up to +14). Enemies with <= 16 life hit harder too.
quirks.why: Each attack record has two variance rows; the code picks the second one when the ATTACKER's life is <= 16 ($7eee).

shots.caption: Desperation damage for everyone

quirks.title: The 3-hit chain has a hole
quirks.do: Between chain link 1 and link 2 the soldier is back in its normal state for 3 frames, so the 'combo' is not guaranteed.
quirks.why: Link 1's flinch ends 11 f after contact, link 2 needs 14 f to connect (buffered press + 4 f startup).

shots.caption: The 3-hit chain has a hole

quirks.title: Stun meter that forgets to refresh
quirks.do: Any 3 quick hits knock a soldier down, but hits spread out never do, and two hits just before the meter expires plus one after do not either.
quirks.why: The decay timer is only set by the first hit (50/60/80 f); later hits add to the meter without resetting the timer ($17b2).

shots.caption: Stun meter that forgets to refresh

quirks.title: Specials make the game easier
quirks.do: Every special that hits costs 6 life but also lowers the hidden difficulty rank (enemy damage and toughness).
quirks.why: The special code subtracts 32/256 from the rank word $FF7FA6 when it connects ($1a216).

shots.caption: Specials make the game easier

quirks.title: Random command window
quirks.do: The DOWN-then-UP command sometimes works with a slow UP and sometimes not.
quirks.why: After the DOWN charge the window for UP is drawn at random (8-15 frames, table $1F5C) on every attempt.

shots.caption: Random command window

quirks.title: Arrows weaken in flight
quirks.do: Huang Zhong's arrows do 10 close up, 9 after ~8 frames of flight, 8 after ~14.
quirks.why: The arrow object swaps its attack record (rec $6F0 -> $700 -> $710) as it flies.

shots.caption: Arrows weaken in flight

quirks.title: Command move out of a grab
quirks.do: Charging DOWN while holding an enemy, then UP+B, drops the enemy and does the rising command attack (Wei Yan gets a different 2-hit version from a hold).
quirks.why: The command detector ($1f7c) runs every frame for every state, and the hold code checks it.

shots.caption: Command move out of a grab

quirks.title: Debug leftovers
quirks.do: Two RAM bytes left from development: $FF6391 picks the starting round (a stage select) and $FF6393 bit 0 makes players untouchable.
quirks.why: Read at game start ($ae40) and in every enemy-vs-player hit loop ($8730, $91da).

shots.caption: Debug leftovers

quirks.why: $19930: x += table $19962[direction] (0,16,32,16,0,-16,-32,-16) when the dive starts; +$C2 = $FFFF
$95FC8: if the victim is not attacker+$F0 the damage is halved before the defence multiplier; the Mega Crash (reaction $80) skips this and hits everyone for the same flat 16
$189A0: life = max(life - 10, 0); death is only checked when an enemy hit lands; $1891A branches to the grenade at 0 life
$20C1A / $20C80: the air attack adds $100 to the x speed in the facing direction, even with no jump direction
$96C8C: the victim shakes for 6 frames (+$4C) before its own hit-stop counter starts
$18114: +$D5 records jump presses as a shift register during the fall; any of the last 4 frames set -> immediate re-jump
$202AC: in the air, a fresh press with a direction tests the map 4 px ahead ($ACF0E == $80 wall) and jumps to $1A124
$1D104: only direction code 4 (down) / none goes to the knee, everything else to $1D2F6
$1D200: damage is subtracted directly, no box test, counter +$A2
$17CBE: chain credit >= 40, victim standing and grabbable -> forced grab state with the throw selected
act $14 handler $184F4 is never set by the input code I traced; anims 71/72 sit on +$0E values no code writes

quirks.title: Apex dive kick
quirks.do: Neutral jump and press B exactly at the top of the jump (height >= 76 px for Jack, 75 Mustapha, 93 Hannah, 72 Mess).
quirks.happens: Instead of the normal jump attack the character dives forward 130-190 px with the attack box out until landing (15 damage, hit-stop 6). Forward jumps of Jack, Hannah and Mess never reach the threshold, so only a neutral jump (or Mustapha's forward jump) can do it.
quirks.why: The air code compares the height above ground with a per-character pair of words ($1A734: 16 / threshold): >= threshold picks the dive state 0200/04/0A ($1A9A4), else the low attack. The threshold sits within 1-2 px of each character's neutral apex.
quirks.brawler: A one-button 'timing' move: same input, different attack by height. Cheap to copy and gives jumps skill depth.

shots.caption: Apex dive kick

quirks.title: Holding B fires the jump attack by itself
quirks.do: Hold B and press A (or keep B held from a special attempt) and stay holding.
quirks.happens: The jump attack comes out automatically as soon as the character is 16 px above the ground.
quirks.why: The jump-attack check tests the HELD attack bit (+$A0 bit 4), not the fresh press ($1A704).
quirks.brawler: Accidental auto-attacks; if copying, test the fresh-press bit.

shots.caption: Holding B fires the jump attack by itself

quirks.title: Combo throw out of the chain
quirks.do: Hold UP or DOWN while pressing B for the 4th link of the punch chain.
quirks.happens: Instead of the finisher the character grabs and throws the enemy (throw damage, invulnerable during the throw).
quirks.why: Link 4 checks the victim: if it is already back in its normal state and the stick is UP or DOWN without left/right, the code jumps into the throw handler ($195B2 -> $1D888).
quirks.brawler: Same branch idea as Warriors of Fate (UP/DOWN at link 2), here at link 4.

shots.caption: Combo throw out of the chain

quirks.title: The chain survives a pause
quirks.do: Hit with a jab, let go, wait more than half a second (up to ~38 frames) after the recoil ends, press B again.
quirks.happens: The next link (not link 1) comes out: you can space the chain out and still get the finisher.
quirks.why: After each connected link a 40-frame chain credit (+$AE) runs while idle; any B press inside it resumes at the stored hit count (+$B2) ($191B4 -> $194D4). Walking is only blocked for the first 4 frames.
quirks.brawler: A forgiving combo rule; lets players re-position on depth between links.

shots.caption: The chain survives a pause

quirks.title: Jab cancel spam on whiff
quirks.do: Mash B in the air (no enemy) every 3 frames.
quirks.happens: Jack, Hannah and Mustapha restart the jab continuously from its recovery frames; Mess's jab plays out fully each time.
quirks.why: Recovery records with byte 4 = 1 allow a fresh B to restart the jab with anim 1 ($19446 -> $193DE); Mess's jab script lacks that record flag in the window the mash hits.
quirks.brawler: Whiff cancels make the light attack a wall; decide deliberately per character.

shots.caption: Jab cancel spam on whiff

quirks.title: Command move from a hold kills a common enemy
quirks.do: Grab an enemy, then DOWN, UP + B.
quirks.happens: The character releases the hold into the full multi-hit command move; a 44-life Ferris dies every time (more than a throw, which does 20-30).
quirks.why: The hold handler checks the command flag (+$F1 = 2, set by the input reader $6AC8) before anything else and jumps to the command move ($1D652 -> $1B6EC); all its hits land on the released victim.
quirks.brawler: A strong 'throw variant' for free; no life cost unlike the A+B special.

shots.caption: Command move from a hold kills a common enemy

quirks.title: Only Mess has a real back throw
quirks.do: Grab with each character and press away + B.
quirks.happens: Jack, Hannah and Mustapha turn round and play their forward throw; Mess plays a different, longer back-throw animation (47 f vs 41 f).
quirks.why: The throw code picks anim 4 vs 3 only for character 3 ($1D854); the others set the facing from the stick and use anim 3.
quirks.brawler: Unique throws are a cheap way to give the heavy his identity.

shots.caption: Only Mess has a real back throw

quirks.title: Special is free on whiff and can't kill you
quirks.do: Use A+B with nobody in reach, then with one enemy in reach, at 100 life.
quirks.happens: Whiff: life stays 100. One contact: 100 -> 90. Further contacts cost 4 each, at most 18 per special, and never take the last point.
quirks.why: The cost is applied in the hit handler (class 6 attacks, $10B08) from a 20-point budget +$EE (10 first, then 4); life is clamped to 1.
quirks.brawler: Captain Commando-like 'pay on contact' rule; make the special a safe escape.

shots.caption: Special is free on whiff and can't kill you

quirks.title: Commands cancel the hit-stop
quirks.do: land a chain link, then input →A / ↓↘A / ↓↑A / A+J during the 8-frame freeze
quirks.happens: the freeze ends at once and the special starts on the next frame
quirks.why: command handlers ($3733C, $37366, $373F4) clear the attacker hit-stop byte +$53 before switching state; the recognizer ($F157C) runs before the hit-stop skip in the player loop ($352F4)
quirks.brawler: a cancel that also skips the freeze makes routes feel fast; if we copy the cancel rule, decide explicitly whether hit-stop is kept

shots.caption: Commands cancel the hit-stop

quirks.title: Running is an attack (0-damage tackle)
quirks.do: run (→→) into an enemy
quirks.happens: no damage, the enemy is knocked off its feet and the runner hops back
quirks.why: every frame of the run animation carries attack box $2D with attack type 3; the hit code ($26316/$263FC) turns a type-3 contact into ctx 18 (bounce, T1 anim 31/28/25) and a knockdown on the victim
quirks.brawler: a free knock-down on contact is a strong crowd tool; we would need a cost (no damage already) or a cooldown

shots.caption: Running is an attack (0-damage tackle)

quirks.title: Hold attack = push-away follow-up
quirks.do: keep A held through a chain link that hits
quirks.happens: instead of the next link the character does a slow shove/strike (2-3 dmg, attack type 2) that blows the enemy away
quirks.why: +$74 = 6-frame hold window, +$75 set if A is released; link end with +$75=0 and +$70 hit flag -> state +7=4, anim T1 26 ($3E8DE)
quirks.brawler: a cheap "ring-out" option inside the chain; reads as a deliberate spacing tool

shots.caption: Hold attack = push-away follow-up

quirks.title: Air hits freeze the victim at its height
quirks.do: hit an airborne enemy (↓↑A then A in the air, or a ground link on a falling enemy)
quirks.happens: the enemy hangs in the air for the whole hit-stun (y stays e.g. 120), then continues/relaunches
quirks.why: hit reaction sets +4=4/+6=2 (stagger) without gravity; only launch reactions (+6=4) move it
quirks.brawler: this is what makes DDSOM juggles readable without a juggle counter: the limit is drift and fall time, not a cap

shots.caption: Air hits freeze the victim at its height

quirks.title: Plunge re-hits the same enemy
quirks.do: jump and press ↓+A over an enemy
quirks.happens: the plunge hits once, keeps its box out to the floor and hits the same enemy again when its stun ends
quirks.why: one hit per hit-id per victim is enforced through the victim slot +$58[attacker]; the enemy reaction clears +$58 when its stun ends ($74212 clrl +$58), so the same box can land again
quirks.brawler: long-lived boxes become multi-hit automatically; we must reset hit memory per move, not per stun

shots.caption: Plunge re-hits the same enemy

quirks.title: Mega Crush only costs life on contact, never kills
quirks.do: A+J with an enemy in range vs in the air
quirks.happens: 12 life is removed at the end of the first hit-stop; whiffed Mega Crush is free; life is floored at 1; the Cleric never pays
quirks.why: $3F00C: if +$58 bit0 (hit landed) and +$1EC not yet set: life -= 12, if <= 0 then 1
quirks.brawler: a desperation move that cannot kill you and is free on whiff = an invincible (whole move has no hurt box) panic button

shots.caption: Mega Crush only costs life on contact, never kills

quirks.title: Magic-User glides on a run-jump
quirks.do: run (→→) then jump with the Magic-User
quirks.happens: the jump lasts 70+ air frames instead of 47 (slow fall)
quirks.why: measured: same peak 63 px, the fall stretches (runjump capture); MU-specific jump code
quirks.brawler: per-character air control is cheap variety

shots.caption: Magic-User glides on a run-jump

quirks.title: Thief and Magic-User back hop is fully invulnerable
quirks.do: J, J quickly (second press during the pre-jump)
quirks.happens: Thief / Magic-User flip back with no hurt box for 30-32 frames (Fighter/Cleric/Elf hop keeps theirs)
quirks.why: their back-hop animation records carry hurt id 0
quirks.brawler: a defensive escape with a real invincibility window gives the light characters an identity

shots.caption: Thief and Magic-User back hop is fully invulnerable

quirks.title: Vary your specials for loot
quirks.do: land different specials in a row (↓↘A, then ↓↑A, then Mega Crush) on one enemy
quirks.happens: that enemy is more likely to drop an item when it goes down
quirks.why: each special hit whose ctx differs from the attacker's previous special (+$5B) adds 1 to the victim's +$9C; the drop check $B648 rolls rand(32) against a mask with +$9C bits set (n/32)
quirks.brawler: a reward for variety instead of a penalty for repetition

shots.caption: Vary your specials for loot

quirks.title: A changes meaning next to tall or downed enemies
quirks.do: press A next to a tall enemy (probe box 1, 96-128 px up) or next to a downed one (probe box 2, 0-24 px up)
quirks.happens: vs tall enemies the chain switches to high slashes (ctx 2, T1 5/6, code only); next to a downed Goblin the Fighter kneels over it (ctx 4, T0 39, 18 f, no attack box): lying enemies cannot be hit
quirks.why: $371A tests attack boxes 1 and 2 of the character box set against every enemy hurt box (box 2 only against enemies flagged down +$86) before choosing the context
quirks.brawler: context-sensitive normals make one button cover everything; DDSOM also uses it to make lying enemies untouchable (no OTG)

shots.caption: A changes meaning next to tall or downed enemies

quirks.title: Two-handed weapon halves the Fighter chain
quirks.do: Fighter with weapon slot B (+$10E) below 40 (no shield)
quirks.happens: the chain becomes 2 heavy links (T1 38/39, 2 hits each) instead of 4
quirks.why: $3E8C0: anim = 38 + link if +$10E < 40, max link index 2 instead of 4
quirks.brawler: equipment that rewrites the chain: a real build choice

shots.caption: Two-handed weapon halves the Fighter chain
